sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `pi`. [claim-pi-agent-harness-identity]
- Canonical name: Pi. [claim-pi-agent-harness-identity]
- Repository locator: `badlogic/pi-mono` is the same GitHub repo as `earendil-works/pi` (id 1035029907). [claim-pi-sf-pi-mono-same-repo]
- Current status: the canonical repository was not archived; repository metadata recorded a 2026-08-09 push, while the release page recorded v0.84.1 on 2026-08-07. [claim-pi-repository-status] [claim-pi-maintenance-signal] [claim-pi-release-version]
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-09. [claim-pi-agent-harness-identity]

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: Pi describes itself as a minimal terminal coding harness and self-extensible coding agent. [claim-pi-minimal-terminal-positioning]
- What it is not: Pi core does not include subagents, plan mode, MCP, permission popups, to-dos, or background bash; extensions or external tools may add such behavior. [claim-pi-built-in-omissions]

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` is a project-taxonomy inference from first-party loop ownership. [claim-pi-primary-type-runtime]
- Agent-loop owner: `pi-agent-core` owns provider calls, tool execution, steering, follow-up, and turn completion. [claim-pi-agent-loop-owner]
- Architecture: the repository separates the coding-agent CLI, agent core, provider API, and terminal UI packages. [claim-pi-package-architecture]

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-pi-cli-interactive`, `surface-pi-cli-print-json`, `surface-pi-rpc`, `surface-pi-sdk`, `surface-pi-termux`, `surface-pi-windows-cli`, and `surface-pi-remote-session-api`. [claim-pi-minimal-terminal-positioning] [claim-pi-api-modes] [claim-pi-rpc-interface] [claim-pi-sdk-interface] [claim-pi-termux-route] [claim-pi-windows-bash-requirement] [claim-pi-remote-server-boundary]
- Execution location: the default agent and tools run on the same device in the current project directory with the launching user's permissions. [claim-pi-local-execution]
- Windows compatibility: Pi requires a bash shell and documents the lookup order for a custom path, Git Bash, and `bash.exe` on `PATH`. [claim-pi-windows-bash-requirement]

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: each Pi provider owns its catalog, authentication, and stream behavior; Pi routes the selected request to that provider. [claim-pi-provider-owned-routing]
- Auth strategy: Pi documents subscription login for Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT Plus/Pro Codex, and GitHub Copilot, plus CLI, environment, and local-file API-key paths. [claim-pi-subscription-auth] [claim-pi-api-key-auth]
- Provider support: first-party code lists many direct, cloud, gateway, and OpenAI-compatible providers; local-model paths are documented, but exact live availability was not tested. [claim-pi-provider-support] [claim-pi-local-model-support]

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: Pi can transform agent messages before converting them for the selected provider. [claim-pi-context-transform]
- Memory: session history and extension state are supported; a separate built-in semantic-memory service remains unknown. [claim-pi-memory-boundary]
- Compaction: automatic near-limit compaction and manual `/compact` are documented. [claim-pi-compaction]
- Session behavior: Pi stores append-only JSONL session trees and supports continue, resume, tree navigation, fork, and clone. [claim-pi-session-storage] [claim-pi-session-branching]

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: read, write, edit, and bash are default model tools; grep, find, and ls are extra read-only options. [claim-pi-built-in-tools]
- Extensions: trusted TypeScript modules can add tools, commands, providers, UI, hooks, and session behavior. [claim-pi-extension-model]
- MCP: built-in MCP is unsupported; extension-supplied MCP behavior remains unknown. [claim-pi-mcp-boundary]
- Skills: Pi implements Agent Skills discovery and on-demand loading. [claim-pi-skills-support]
- Hooks: extensions can intercept context, provider requests, tool calls/results, compaction, and session lifecycle. [claim-pi-hook-support]
- APIs: official modes include print/JSON, local JSONL RPC, and an embedding SDK. [claim-pi-api-modes] [claim-pi-rpc-interface] [claim-pi-sdk-interface]

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: core Pi omits built-in subagents and plan mode; extensions may add behavior. [claim-pi-built-in-omissions]
- Parallelism: the agent loop runs tool calls in parallel unless configured as sequential; this does not establish parallel-agent orchestration. [claim-pi-orchestration-boundary]

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: Pi has no built-in sandbox; stronger isolation relies on external infrastructure. [claim-pi-no-built-in-sandbox]
- Permissions: Pi has no built-in filesystem, process, network, or credential restriction system; by default it runs with the permissions of the user and process that launched it. [claim-pi-permission-boundary]
- Security: the project treats the local user, writable files, environment, shell startup files, and Pi configuration as one trust boundary. [claim-pi-security-trust-boundary]
- Data path: default auth, model, settings, resource, and session state lives under `~/.pi/agent`; provider requests leave that local path for the chosen endpoint. [claim-pi-local-state-path] [claim-pi-provider-owned-routing]

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-pi-cli-interactive` is the local interactive CLI. [claim-pi-minimal-terminal-positioning]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-pi-cli-print-json` is the local one-shot or machine-readable CLI route. [claim-pi-api-modes]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-pi-rpc` is local JSONL stdin/stdout RPC. [claim-pi-rpc-interface]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-pi-sdk` is an embedding API, not a first-party app. [claim-pi-sdk-interface]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-pi-termux` is same-device Android terminal use, not native mobile. [claim-pi-termux-route]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-pi-windows-cli` is a same-device Windows terminal route that requires bash. [claim-pi-windows-bash-requirement]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-pi-remote-session-api` combines a transport-neutral client with experimental, application-completed server components; it is not a turnkey remote client. [claim-pi-remote-client-components] [claim-pi-remote-server-boundary]
- Remote behavior: vendor relay, end-to-end remote start/resume, and approval semantics remain unknown; client reconnect and authentication are consumer-managed. [claim-pi-vendor-relay-unknown] [claim-pi-remote-client-components] [claim-pi-remote-server-boundary]
- Mobile behavior: Termux is documented; native iOS, native Android graphical, and first-party mobile-web routes remain unknown. [claim-pi-termux-route] [claim-pi-native-mobile-unknown]
- Background behavior: background bash is not built into core Pi. [claim-pi-background-bash-boundary]

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: unknown; checked official paths did not establish a Pi software price or provider billing terms. [claim-pi-pricing-unknown]
- License: MIT. [claim-pi-license-mit]
- Maintenance: repository metadata recorded a 2026-08-09 push; the release page separately recorded v0.84.1 on 2026-08-07. These are dated signals, not a future-maintenance guarantee. [claim-pi-maintenance-signal] [claim-pi-release-version]
- Lock-in: unknown; multi-provider, local-model, custom-endpoint, and MIT evidence does not settle billing or migration dependence. [claim-pi-lock-in-unknown]

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: Pi is the lineage target for Atomic and Oh My Pi forks and for Prime Agent's baseline `built_on` edge. [claim-pi-lineage-neighborhood]
- Relationship edges: existing baseline tuples are `atomic --fork_of--> pi`, `oh-my-pi --fork_of--> pi`, and `prime-agent --built_on--> pi`; this proposal does not recreate them. [claim-pi-lineage-neighborhood]
- Compatibility note: Discord and Telegram access belongs to the separate first-party `pi-chat` extension, not Pi core. [claim-pi-messaging-extension-separate]

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
- Comparison neighborhood IDs: `neighborhood-pi-lineage-terminal-runtimes`, based only on specific Pi lineage or architecture; Pi's staged membership role is `same-lineage`, with Pi retained as the lineage root rather than a core peer. [claim-pi-lineage-neighborhood]
- Substitutes: unknown; lineage does not prove interchangeability. [claim-pi-lineage-neighborhood]
- Partial substitutes: unknown; this documentation wave did not establish shared user constraints or outcome parity. [claim-pi-lineage-neighborhood]
- Same-lineage relatives: Atomic, Oh My Pi, and Prime Agent; their decisive runtime additions remain separate. [claim-pi-lineage-neighborhood]
- Often-confused products: unknown. [claim-pi-lineage-neighborhood]
- Complements: unknown as a comparison-neighborhood membership; `pi-chat` is only recorded as a separate extension route. [claim-pi-messaging-extension-separate]

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: vendor positioning centers on a small, adaptable terminal harness and extension ecosystem rather than a large fixed core. [claim-pi-unique-positioning]
- Meaningful drawbacks: Pi does not build in sandboxing or a permission policy; core also omits subagents, MCP, plan mode, and background bash. [claim-pi-minimal-core-drawback] [claim-pi-built-in-omissions]
- Best fit: Pi is positioned for terminal users who want to configure or extend their coding harness. [claim-pi-intended-user]
- Not-for: users who require those omitted features as built-in defaults; extension availability must not be inferred from the omission list. [claim-pi-built-in-omissions]
